learning_objective: 🎯 Step into the world of programming using block-based coding! Create your own interactive stories, animations, and mini-games without typing complex code.

इवेंट (वह क्रिया जो स्क्रिप्ट को शुरू करती है)

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Scratch is a visual programming language. The 'Sprite' is the character (like the famous Scratch Cat), the 'Stage' is the background, and the 'Blocks Palette' contains colorful puzzle pieces representing code.
You program in Scratch by snapping blocks together. A stack of connected blocks is called a 'Script'. The blocks run in order from top to bottom.
Every script needs a trigger to start. The 'Events' blocks (yellow) do this. For example, 'When Green Flag clicked' or 'When Space key pressed' tells the Sprite exactly when to start moving.
You can use visual blocks for logic. The 'Repeat' and 'Forever' blocks are loops. The 'If... Then' block allows the Sprite to make decisions (like 'If touching the wall, then bounce').

fun_activity.title: 🕺 Make the Cat Dance!
fun_activity.instructions: In Scratch, drag a 'When Green flag clicked' block. Attach a 'Forever' loop. Inside the loop, put 'Move 10 steps', 'Next Costume', and 'Play sound Meow'. Click the green flag and watch the cat run and meow endlessly!

exam_tips: 📌 The Scratch Stage is based on an X-Y coordinate grid. The center is (0,0). X goes left/right, Y goes up/down.
📌 Know the color codes: Blue is Motion (movement), Purple is Looks (changing costumes/speaking), Yellow is Events (triggers), and Orange is Control (loops/if-else).
📌 A Sprite can have multiple 'Costumes' which allow you to create animations (like making it look like it's walking).
quick_recap: ⭐ Block-based programming helps you learn logic without worrying about syntax errors (missing commas or brackets).
⭐ The 'Broadcast' block is used to send hidden messages between different sprites to make them talk or interact.
⭐ Scratch is developed by the MIT Media Lab and is entirely free.
